{{La Bangu/en}}
Lojban had 6 words for "and" depending on the syntactical role of "and" in sentence. Namely,

#'''je''' was "and" conjunction for linking parts of compound verbs. (e.g. "quickly <u>and</u> gently run")
#'''.e''' was "and" for linking nouns/pronouns/personal names (My friend <u>and</u> I came home)
#'''zi'e''' was "and" for linking two relative clauses belonging to one noun/pronoun (The king who ruled for 30 years <u>and</u> who died later...)
#'''gi'e''' was "and" for linking two verb phrases belonging to one sentence (I like apples <u>and</u> you like them too).
#'''ge ... gi''' was "and" for forethought connectives (<u>Both</u> you <u>and</u> I like it).
#'''gu'e ... gi''' was "and" for forethought connectives in compound verbs (I run <u>both</u> quickly <u>and</u> gently).

Now since a new formal grammar is implemented in the form of a new grammatical parser for items 1 till 3 only one word '''je''' is enough, the parser will understand where "and" belongs to automatically. Items 4 till 6 can be formed with '''je''' with additional words.

Why so? Because Lojban is based on formal grammar and auxlangs are based on human intuition.

Every time we improve the parser Lojban becomes more and more human-friendly.

Compared to the original Loglan as of 1980 it's a completely reworked language (read e.g. [[Stub: Lojbab about the history of Lojban|Lojbab about the history of Lojban]] for more details. The latest revisions just mentioned are not part of the official Lojban yet; They are called [[La Bangu]] dialect).

But we can't break formal grammar making Lojban an easily learnable auxlang in hope that future parsers will handle it. It just has a different goal.[[Category:La Bangu]]
